The one non-significant endpoint was SDMT (cognitive measure, p=0.4669), suggesting the mechanism may not fully translate to cognitive protection in this timeframe. 4. No subgroup analyses showing differential response were reported beyond the overall population. 5. CONFOUNDERS: Safety signals are notable — TESAEs 11.4% vs 6.9%, infusion-related reactions, pneumonia SAEs (3 vs 0), CNS enteroviral infections (2 vs 0). These are manageable but represent a real safety consideration. No dose-limiting toxicity prevented adequate dosing. The trial was adequately powered (n=549, 96 weeks). The active comparator design (vs teriflunomide) provides a meaningful benchmark. Overall, this is a clear success with strong mechanistic validation across the causal chain.

This is a minor caveat in an otherwise successful trial.
